title: HighDimensionalCorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is a differentiable function f on ℝᵈ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. It may be nonconvex. It has a global lower bound b satisfying f(x₀) − b ≤ Δ.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: One call at x returns a pair (v, w). A clean reply satisfies |v − f(x)| ≤ ε²/(128L). Clean values may vary across repeated queries at x.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: In the same reply, a clean vector w equals g(x) for one fixed hidden field g satisfying ‖g(x) − ∇f(x)‖ ≤ ε/8 for every x. All clean replies at a repeated query therefore return the same vector.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: The clean gradient field may have a persistent additive bias up to ε/8. The accuracy condition is pointwise and allows this bias to persist through repeated calls.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is Euclidean ℝᵈ. With m = ⌊LΔ/(2²⁵ ε²)⌋, validity requires L > 0, ε > 0, LΔ ≥ 2²⁶ ε² and d ≥ 2³²(m + 1)⁴.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Every reachable history contains at most k replies violating either clean-reply condition, counting a jointly corrupted pair once. These replies can be arbitrary and history-dependent. The pathwise limit applies to every reachable seed sequence. The algorithm receives d, L, Δ, ε, k, failure and x₀ as public inputs. The objective and the field g are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.lean, Params, Reachable, errors, accurate, spec.publicInput and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Oracle.answer

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a point x_out ∈ ℝᵈ. Success is measured by the unsquared true gradient norm ‖∇f(x_out)‖ ≤ ε. The output may be any point computed from the final state.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The probability that ‖∇f(x_out)‖ > ε must be at most the public failure parameter in [0, 1/4], under the product of the algorithm-seed law and the oracle-sequence law. A failure parameter of zero requires almost-sure success.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines smooth nonconvex stationarity with a fixed biased gradient field, approximate function values and a shared pathwise budget of k arbitrary joint replies. It also imposes an explicit high-dimensional regime.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Stationarity with Corrupted First-Order Queries

We seek a stationary point to tolerance ε>0 for a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in high dimension d. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz for L>0, and the value at a given starting point is within Δ>0 of a global lower bound. Except for at most k corrupted replies, each query returns an approximate function value and the value of a fixed, uniformly accurate gradient approximation, where k is a nonnegative integer. The goal is an output x¯∈Rd whose Euclidean gradient norm exceeds ε with probability at most δ∈[0,1/4].

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives d, L, Δ, ε, k, δ, and the starting point x0∈Rd. The dimension d is a positive integer, and the parameters satisfy LΔ≥226ε2,d≥232(⌊LΔ225ε2⌋+1)4.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere. With ∥⋅∥ denoting the Euclidean norm, its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd. There exists ℓ∈R such that f(x)≥ℓ for every x∈Rd and f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Corrupted first-order replies). There exists a fixed map g:Rd→Rd satisfying ∥g(x)−∇f(x)∥≤ε8,x∈Rd. At any query point x∈Rd, the oracle returns a pair (v,w)∈R×Rd. A reply is accurate if both conditions hold: |v−f(x)|≤ε2128L,w=g(x). Replies may depend on previous queries and replies. For every finite query sequence and every choice of oracle randomness along it, at most k replies fail the accuracy conditions.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must satisfy P(∥∇f(x¯)∥>ε)≤δ, where P is the joint law of the independent algorithm and oracle randomness.

theorems.formulaHtml: k+⌊L⋅Δ225⋅ε2⌋+

comparisonHtml:
Let f:Rd→R have L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0)−inff≤Δ, with L,ε>0. Assume T≥226 and d≥232(1+⌊T/225⌋)4. A randomized algorithm may query anywhere. Along every history, all replies except at most k at query points x have the form (v,g(x)), where |v−f(x)|≤ε2/(128L) and a fixed g satisfies ∥g(x)−∇f(x)∥≤ε/8 everywhere. The target is Pr∗(∥∇f(xout)∥>ε)≤δ for prescribed 0≤δ≤1/4.

Lower bounds for finding a stationary point with corrupted first-order replies
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) CorruptedFirstOrderLowerBound (Ours) (review) Lower bound: Ω(k+LΔ/ε2) joint value–gradient calls.
(2) (Carmon et al. 2020, Thm. 2)
Randomized, exact oracle, k=0		 Lower bound: Ω(LΔ/ε2) all-derivative calls. (1) extends (2) by prefixing k uninformative replies, formalizing the clean-rate extension. The additive k dominates when k≫T. (1) needs quartic dimension versus d≳T2log⁡T in (2). It covers first-order access and failure at the returned point. (2) covers all derivatives and all iterates through the budget.
(3) (Carmon et al. 2020, Thm. 1)
Deterministic, exact oracle, k=0		 Lower bound: Ω(LΔ/ε2) all-derivative calls. (1) extends hardness to randomized algorithms and matches (3) on the clean deterministic restriction. (1) needs quartic dimension. For deterministic algorithms, prefixing (3) with k uninformative replies already gives the derived bound Ω(k+LΔ/ε2) in dimension d≳T.

Abbr: T=LΔ/ε2; Pr∗ denotes outer probability; Ω denotes a necessary budget up to a universal factor.

Carmon, Yair, John C. Duchi, Oliver Hinder, and Aaron Sidford. 2020. “Lower Bounds for Finding Stationary Points I.” Mathematical Programming 184: 71–120. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-019-01406-y.

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalCorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex

abbrev spec : Setup := { CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.spec with
  valid := fun (p : CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.Params) => 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 2 ^ 26 * p.ε ^ 2 ≤ p.L * p.Δ ∧
    2 ^ 32 * (⌊p.L * p.Δ / (2 ^ 25 * p.ε ^ 2)⌋₊ + 1) ^ 4 ≤ p.d }

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalCorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex
